title: Physics-Informed Lambda/4n Initialization with Relaxed 35nm Minimum Thickness
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses at lambda/(4n) scaled to both band centers (550nm for visible, 850nm for NIR) rather than uniform random or single-wavelength quarter-wave will anchor phase alignment from the start, reducing optimizer search distance and preventing local minima associated with interference-sensitive thin layers.
design_principle: Quarter-wave baseline initialization at dual band centers, then gradient refinement with relaxed minimum thickness bound to prevent layer collapse during optimization.
proposed_topology: 24-layer alternating stack: TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2|TiO2|SiO2 on fused silica substrate, terminated with SiO2
design_variables: initialization centered on lambda/(4n) at 550nm and 850nm
manufacturing_considerations: minimum thickness 35nm relaxed from 30nm to prevent collapse
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack provides physically motivated starting point for local optimization
Dual-band center initialization anchors phase for both target bands simultaneously
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to better initialization
Better phase alignment for both bands from start
known_risks: Dual-band initialization may create conflicting phase requirements
May not outperform single-band quarter-wave if one band dominates merit function
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating TiO2/SiO2 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate at 45-degree incidence. Initialize layer thicknesses using physics-informed lambda/(4n) scaling: for TiO2 layers use n~2.47, for SiO2 layers use n~1.46, with design wavelengths centered at 550nm (visible band center) and 850nm (NIR band center). Set minimum thickness bound to 35nm (relaxed from 30nm), maximum bound to 200nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer with soft objectives: maximize reflectance in 450-650nm band, maximize transmittance in 700-1000nm band, minimize crosstalk (suppress transmittance in 450-650nm and reflectance in 700-1000nm). Evaluate unpolarized or both s- and p-polarization states. Output best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm array for all candidates. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 450-650 nm, 700-1000 nm. soft objectives: high reflectance in 450-650 nm; high transmittance in 700-1000 nm; minimized crosstalk between bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 450-650 nm; reflectance in 700-1000 nm. manufacturing constraints: maximum 24 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive: relax minimum thickness bound by +5nm (30nm to 35nm) and replace uniform random initialization with physics-informed lambda/(4n) scaling centered on both spectral bands to anchor phase alignment from optimization start.
